extracted.intended_audience: experimental physicists / natural philosophers; students and practitioners performing classical fluid-resistance experiments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for designing, conducting, and interpreting experiments on bodies falling through fluids (air, water, mercury), including timing, apparatus corrections, and theoretical caveats about fluid resistance and wave propagation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sufficiently heavy bodies for reliable measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pondus globi in aqua debet esse plurium granorum, ut experimentum certum & fide dignum reddatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the mass of the test spheres appreciable (several grains in the context) so measurement uncertainty and perturbations (bubbles, weighing errors) are small relative to the weight; small masses yield uncertain results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control temperature and material rarefaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Globi, ubi ponderabantur & postea cadebant, frigidi erant & aqua quoaddiu frigidi manserant; quia calor ceram rarefacit, & per rarefactionem diminuit pondus globi in aqua.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure spheres are at uniform, low temperature and remain so from weighing to release — heating (e.g., from handling or environment) rarefies wax or other materials, altering buoyancy and producing systematic errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immerse bodies fully before release
rubrics_metrics.description: Antequam caderent, immergebantur penitus in aquam; ne pondere partis alicujus ex aqua extantis descensus sub initio acceleraretur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submerge objects completely before letting them fall so that any transient change in displaced fluid (and thus buoyant force) does not cause an initial spurious acceleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release without imparting impulse
rubrics_metrics.description: Et ubi penitus immersi quiescebant, demittebantur quam cautissime, ne impulsum a manu demittente acciperent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a careful release technique to avoid imparting any extra push or torque; impulses at release distort the measured fall times and velocities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat trials and use modal/most-frequent values; note environmental changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimento saepius capto, globi ceciderunt maxima ex parte temporibus oscillationum ... Iteravi experimentum a die; sed tempestas jam paulo frigidior erat ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform many repeats, record each trial, and use the most representative (e.g., most frequent) timings. Track environmental variables (temperature, weather) between runs because they affect results; repeat under comparable conditions when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct for confinement and vessel geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Ob angustiam vasis nostri, minuatur hoc spatium in ratione quae componitur ex subduplicata ratione orificii vasis ad excessum hujus orificii supra semicirculum maximum globi, & simplici ratione ejusdem orificii ad excessum ejus supra circulum maximum globi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for reduced effective travel and altered flow when the container is narrow compared to the sphere. Apply geometric corrections relating vessel opening and sphere diameter to obtain the theoretical (unconfined) displacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid or account for side collisions and wall impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ubi tardius cecidere, suspicor eosdem retardatos fuisse impingendo in latera vasis. ... nonnunquam audivi impulsum eorum in latera vasis antequam ad fundum pervenerunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure spheres do not touch or strike vessel walls during fall, or record and correct for such collisions since they retard motion and produce non-theoretical timings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce oscillation of falling bodies by asymmetrical weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut oscillatio globorum minor redderetur, globos novos ex cera & plumbo construxi, infigendo plumbum in latus aliquod globi prope superficiem ejus; & globum ita demisi, ut latus gravius, quoad fieri potuit, esset infimum ab initio descensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed a small weight on one side of the sphere so its heavy side faces down at release; this reduces rotational/oscillatory motion and yields more consistent fall times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of attached bubbles, material irregularities, and weighing errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod tardius ceciderunt, utrum minori proportioni resistentiae ... an potius bullulœ nonnullis globo adhaerentibus, vel rarefactioni cerae ... vel etiam erroribus insensibilibus in ponderandis globis in aqua, incertum esse puto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect for and eliminate air bubbles clinging to bodies; ensure accurate weighing and homogeneous construction of spheres to avoid subtle biases; consider these factors when discrepancies arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use calibrated pendulum timing and express times in oscillations
rubrics_metrics.description: Deinde ... demisi ut tempora cadendi in aqua per pendulum, ad semi-minuta secunda oscillans, mensurarem. ... corda ... pendulis ad minuta secunda oscillantibus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure fall times using a well-characterized pendulum (or other calibrated oscillator); record times as counts of oscillations and convert to absolute time using the pendulum period to reduce timing error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct observed times for apparatus-induced delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabula lignea ... tardius devolvebatur quam par erat, & tarda sua devolutlone impediebat descensum globorum sub initio. ... tempora cadendi prorogata fuerunt minutis tertiis octodecim circiter, & jam corrigi debent detrahendo illa minuta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and quantify delays introduced by release apparatus (e.g., a board or latch that moves slowly) and subtract that measured delay from observed fall times, particularly for larger bodies that press differently on the apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistances of equal bodies at equal speeds are proportional to fluid density
rubrics_metrics.description: In  scholio ... ostendimus per experimenta pendulorum quod globorum aequalium & sequivelocium in aere, aqua, & argento vivo motorum resistentiae sunt ut densitates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing media, keep bodies and velocities equal: measured resistive force scales with the density of the surrounding fluid. Note that some experimental setups (e.g., pendulums) may overestimate absolute resistance due to additional sources (string resistance) but the proportionality holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistive force originates from inertia of fluid (proportional to quantity of matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resistentia ... oritur ab inertia materiae & inertiae materiae corporibus essentialis est & quantitati materiae semper proportionalis. ... Per divisionem partium fluidi ... quantitas materiae per divisionem partium ejus non diminuitur; & manente quantitate materiae, manet ejus vis inertiae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model fluid resistance as arising from the inertial reaction of the fluid mass displaced/accelerated by the moving body; subdividing the fluid into finer parts does not eliminate this inertial resistance unless the total fluid mass in the relevant region is reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect deviations from simple quadratic dependence at high speeds and due to shape
rubrics_metrics.description: In motibus tardis resistentia potest esse paulo minor ... In motibus velocibus resistentia potest esse paulo maior, propterea quod elasticitas & compressio fluidi non augeantur in duplicata ratione velocitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the assumed square-law (resistance ∝ velocity^2) may be only approximate: at low speeds shape effects can reduce resistance; at high speeds compressibility/elastic effects of the fluid can make resistance slightly greater than quadratic. Treat these as small corrections to theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer free-fall experiments over pendulums for absolute resistance magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Resistentiae per experimenta pendulorum majores prodierunt (ob causas jam descriptas) quam per experimenta corporum cadentium, idque in ratione 4 ad 3 circiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendulum-based measurements include added resistances (string, support) that inflate measured drag; free-falling sphere experiments give more direct measures of fluid resistance magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure vesicle/sphere diameters by thin-thread circumference method
rubrics_metrics.description: Diametros vesicarum deducebam ex earum circumferentiis filo tenuissimo bis circundato mensuratis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine diameter by measuring circumference with a fine thread wrapped twice and converting using geometry — suitable for soft/irregular objects like inflated vesicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for isochrony of oscillatory fluid motions in U-channels (analogy with pendulum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si aqua in canalis cruribus erectis K L, M N vicibus alternis ascendat & descendet ... dicO quod aqua ascendet & descendet iisdem temporibus quibus pendulum oscillatur. Corol. I: Igitur aquae ascendentis & descendentis ... vices omnes sunt isochronae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing timing/oscillation-based measurements in connected fluid channels, use the pendulum analogy: the reciprocation periods are isochronous (for given effective lengths) and scale with length in the same manner as pendulum periods; use this for calibration or timing of wave/oscillation phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure and motion propagation in fluids diverge and do not follow straight lines except in special alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressio non propagatur per fluidum secundum lineas rectas, nisi ubi particulœ fluidi in directum jacent. ... Motus omnis per fluida propagatus divergit a recto tramite in spatia immota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In modelling wave/pressure transmission through openings or around obstacles, anticipate that pressure and pulses spread (diverge) into surrounding regions rather than propagating strictly along straight rays, because oblique particle interactions cause lateral propagation and diffusion of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vibrating bodies in elastic media produce spherical pulses; in non-elastic media produce circular propagation
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus omne tremulum in medio elastico propagabit motum pulsuum undique in directum; in medio vero non elastico motum circularem excitabit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering sources of waves or sound, account for medium elasticity: elastic media support radial (approximately spherical) pulse propagation from a vibrating body, while non-elastic (yielding) media lead to more circular/flow-like propagation into regions vacated behind the source.
